issues: Five overdoses on one ward could be stopped by nurses by hand: fault now strikes at midnight in eight minutes, too soon to stop every pump, with the library push as the only fix; 'cannot be revived' made clinical; defer cost explicit.

The side-room patient is on the same contaminated line, so he dies either way; ward staff would switch to cylinders; one bulk tank feeding every hospital in a group (5,000 ventilated) is implausible, and a single hospital cannot reach the large scale.

Exposed researcher was dying anyway ('of the infection or when the air runs out'): now a rack collapse with the researcher protected by her suit, killed only by sealing (breathing air cut); defer was free (director in 30 min, harm in an hour), now a 5-minute window; small now an isolated island so five deaths is natural.

Near-duplicate of kept b020 (release a medical product that kills one to prevent five); fatal-reaction rate inconsistent across scales (1 in a dorm vs 3 in a province) and implausible for chemoprophylaxis; no stated cost of a 3-hour defer.

Logic flaw: the one patient is on the contaminated lot too, so she dies either way; any other IV fluid substitutes; island clinic appears from nowhere in a regional-service setting; same stop-a-drip skeleton as b042.
Gassing the hall cannot clean product already packed, and simply holding the dawn shipment saves everyone with no sacrifice; the dilemma collapses.

Five people in the depot's own control building could be phoned or could shelter: few-of-many now radio-less contractors on the jetty; 'solvent' made a toxic liquid; fitter's silence explained (steel walls block radio) so he is not possibly dead already; large tank kept the same so only the downwind population scales.

Fishing boat with a stability computer is implausible: small now a research vessel; deckhand in a ballast tank now an engineer in a pump room with a jammed hatch; defer window made explicit (valves within 2 minutes, captain free in 5); odd 'spring survey' evidence replaced; capsize victims now below decks.
Oil-slick vapour does not poison coastal residents to death, nor could it kill 5,000 in a town, and in-situ burn smoke killing a keeper is implausible; no natural rescale.

Near-duplicate of kept b035 (close a fire door, shutting one person in with the fire) and of b048/b005 (toxic plume over village/town); the picker is in the burning bay with no stated way out, so open doors may not save him.
An emergency-call outage cannot plausibly kill 150 in a city or 4,000 in a region overnight; deferring 25 minutes was not shown to cost the whole night; no natural rescale.
Logic flaw: the spur farmhouse is in the valley that loses gas anyway, so he dies either way; near-duplicate of kept b033 (shed one block in a freeze, killing a dependent man at a farmhouse).
Near-duplicate of kept b033 (shed a grid load that powers one life-dependent person); cardiac bypass in a rural clinic and three hospitals with failed generators mid-bypass at once are implausible.
